items.title: POCUS Made Easy: CLUE Protocol
items.summary: The short cardiopulmonary look, for the shifts where a full RUSH is more scan than the patient has time for.

_homepage.note: CLUE pairs a basic echo with a lung exam and stops there, which is a different tool from the RUSH and I-RUSH protocols already sitting in the feed rather than a lesser version of them. For CCPU purposes it is a useful contrast case: same windows, deliberately narrower question, and a clear account of what you give up by not scanning further. Kimura's original 2011 paper is cited at the bottom if the derivation matters.

items.title: Melô do Embaixador: Brazilian Soul, Funk & Disco Covers
items.summary: Twenty-seven Brazilian readings of the soul and funk canon that takes up most of a shelf at home.

_homepage.note: The collection runs deep on the American originals here — James Brown, Curtis Mayfield, Parliament, Solomon Burke, and the Daptone descendants in Sharon Jones and Menahan Street Band. This is that same material passed through Brazilian studios between 1968 and 2015, sometimes translated into Portuguese, sometimes cut instrumental, sometimes sung in wonderfully approximate English. Tim Maia anchors it, but the anonymous studio bands and disco cash-ins are the reason to stay.

items.title: The Witcher 4 Finally Gets a Launch Window
items.summary: CD Projekt Red puts a year on the Ciri game, and it is further out than anyone was hoping.

_homepage.note: Nowakowski confirmed a 2028 target in a video posted ahead of Gamescom, and the game skipped the show entirely — no gameplay, no trailer. That reframes the Witcher 3 Remastered coverage already in the feed: the free remaster on 29 September and the Songs of the Past expansion in 2027 are now the whole Witcher plan for the next two years, not a warm-up act. Worth knowing before deciding whether to start another Blood and Wine run.

items.title: Hi-Con IR: Bringing Back True IR on Film
items.summary: Genuinely new emulsion rather than another house-branded respool of something that already exists.

_homepage.note: True infrared has been effectively gone from the film market since Kodak and Efke stopped making it, and most things sold as IR since are extended-red films that fake the look. This is the account of getting an actual IR-sensitive stock back into production — the coating problems, the handling constraints, why nobody else bothered. Emulsion news of the kind that is worth more than the tenth camera review of the month.

items.title: How I Meter Slide Film
items.summary: A working method for the one film stock where getting the exposure wrong costs you the frame outright.

_homepage.note: Omar Tibi's argument is that slide film asks you to invert the habit negative film teaches: protect the highlights, let the shadows fall. He shoots it without bracketing on cost grounds and explains how he gets away with that, which is the part most slide-film writing skips. Concrete enough to take out on the next roll rather than nod along to.

items.title: To squeeze or not to squeeze: the ARISE-FLUIDS trial
items.summary: A full appraisal of the one recent septic shock trial actually run in the departments he works in.

_homepage.note: ARISE-FLUIDS randomised early vasopressors against a larger fluid load in Australian, New Zealand and Irish emergency departments, so the case mix and the staffing are his, not an American ICU's. The feed already carries EMCrit 428, which passes over the trial in a roundup, and the 2026 Surviving Sepsis guidelines, which kept the 30 mL/kg suggestion anyway; this is the version that sits with the numbers long enough to say what the two arms actually received. Worth reading before the next time someone asks why the bag is still running.

items.title: ECG Case 130 — ECG Top 100 Self-Assessment Quiz
items.summary: A narrow-complex tachycardia in a well 25-year-old, and a notch in the inferior R waves explaining why she was ever going to get one.

_homepage.note: The Crochetage sign only exists for you if someone has pointed it out once: notching at the apex of the R wave in II, III and aVF, 92–100% specific for a secundum ASD when it appears in all three leads. Put it beside the RVH voltage and the incomplete RBBB and you have a structural diagnosis off a 12-lead in someone who looks entirely well. It sits directly against the ultrasound material already in the pool — this is the ECG that should make you reach for the probe.

items.title: Beyond The Tracks — How Railroading Impacted American Workwear
items.summary: Where the pocket placement, the stripe and the cut of every chore coat in the wardrobe actually came from.

_homepage.note: The feed already carries the chore coat, bleu de travail and flannel histories; this is the American railroad half of the same story, with companies ordering matched ensembles of cloth and print until uniformity for trainmen was standard practice by 1900. It is the origin of hickory stripe and of the silhouette RRL and Pendleton keep redrawing every few seasons. Read it as provenance for things already owned rather than as a shopping list.

items.title: Daptone Records Keeps Classic Soul and R&B Alive
items.summary: Four artists on your shelves record for this label, and the piece is about the tape machine they all pass through.

_homepage.note: Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings, Menahan Street Band, Thee Sacred Souls and Jalen Ngonda are all Daptone or its imprints — a meaningful slice of the soul end of the collection running through one Brooklyn house band and one analogue chain. The twenty-five-year mark is the excuse; the substance is Gabe Roth and Neal Sugarman still refusing to leave tape while everything around them went to the grid. If you have ever wondered why those four records sound like siblings, this is the reason.

items.title: Transmissions: Sun Ra — Door of the Cosmos
items.summary: An hour that opens the far door of jazz without asking you to buy anything first.

_homepage.note: Night Train and the Milt Jackson–Ray Charles date are the collection's centre of gravity in jazz: swinging, tonal, comfortable. Sun Ra is the other edge of the same century, and a conversation with documentary director Drew DeNicola — plus rare Arkestra recordings and Moor Mother reading from The Immeasurable Equation — is a far gentler way in than starting on the discography cold. Aquarium Drunkard is already the deep-listening source in this feed; this is the episode to test that edge on.

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine: New Gameplay, Story Details From State of Play
items.summary: Insomniac's PS5 exclusive lands 15 September — the same day Dragonwilds leaves early access, so one of them waits.

_homepage.note: This is the State of Play showing with actual gameplay and story detail rather than the original teaser: Insomniac's first M-rated game, built only for PS5 with no cross-gen version. The 15 September date collides exactly with RuneScape: Dragonwilds 1.0, which is already in the feed — same day, same console, two very different games. Worth watching before deciding which one gets the fortnight.

items.title: Just a Sec
items.summary: The 1/focal-length rule was invented by somebody else's hands; this is how to find your own number.

_homepage.note: Geoff Chaplin takes the hand-held shutter-speed rule apart and tests the thing nobody bothers to test: the threshold is personal, and yours is probably not 1/50 on a 50mm. That matters far more on film than digital, where there is no stabilisation to hide behind and no chimping to tell you the frame was soft until the scans come back. It costs one roll to establish and then you stop guessing at the bottom end in low light.

items.title: EMCrit 427 — Advancing Concepts in Shock Physiology
items.summary: Two papers that reframe shock as four interfaces rather than one number, which changes what you do with the pressor.

_homepage.note: Rola, Kattan and Siuba's four-interface model splits resuscitation into macrocirculation, venous return, the microcirculation and the tissue itself, and argues each deserves its own target rather than a single MAP. This is the conceptual scaffolding underneath the RUSH exam already in the feed: the exam tells you which interface is broken, this tells you why that distinction matters at the bedside. Worth the hour if you want the CCPU physiology to hang together instead of sitting as a list of views.

items.title: Goodbye "Massive" and "Submassive"
items.summary: The two words you have used for every PE handover since medical school are gone; this is the short version of what replaced them.

_homepage.note: Nickson walks the new AHA/ACC A-to-E clinical categories and why "submassive" was too blunt to hold both the hypoxic patient who is sliding and the well one with a nudged troponin. This is the terminology half of the change that EMCrit's 2026 crashing PE update — already in the feed — handles on the management side. Category A going home from the department is the line that will surprise people.

items.title: Film Photography News — August 2026 Recap
items.summary: A month of film-stock news in one pass: what is actually being coated, and what you will be able to buy in six months.

_homepage.note: Analog.Cafe's monthly recaps track the supply side — coating lines, discontinuations, price moves — rather than camera launches, which is the half of the news that changes what goes in the fridge. Kodak's Ektacolor and Ektapan announcements and Harman's colour-negative experiments both landed this year, so the emulsion side is genuinely moving for the first time in a while. Read it for what to stock up on.

items.title: 50 Vinyl Pressings That Ruin the Streaming and CD Versions
items.summary: A buying list for the narrow case where a specific pressing genuinely beats the file, rather than another vinyl-is-warmer argument.

_homepage.note: The value is the specificity — named pressings, not formats in the abstract — which is the only question that matters once a catalogue title has been reissued five times and they all look the same on Discogs. With 297 records already in, most future additions are repeat pressings of things streaming already covers, so the mastering is the whole difference. Worth a scan before the next order.

items.title: EMCrit 428 — A Few Things: ARISE Fluids, Bicarb and More
items.summary: ARISE FLUIDS was run in Australian and New Zealand emergency departments, so its answer on early vasopressors lands in your resus bay rather than someone else's.

_homepage.note: The trial randomised a thousand patients across ANZ and Ireland and found restricted fluids with early vasopressors no better on days alive and out of hospital — which neither vindicates the 30 mL/kg mandate nor kills it. Weingart pairs the result with the bicarbonate literature in one sitting. Reads directly against the 2026 Surviving Sepsis guidelines episode already in the feed.

items.title: EMCrit 429 — RUSH 2.0: The I-RUSH and CRUSH Exams
items.summary: The RUSH exam re-cut as a standing hemodynamic map rather than a crash-only protocol — the version worth learning before the next CCPU sitting.

_homepage.note: Weingart's rebuild folds LVOT VTI and the interface model of hemodynamics into a scan you run on any undifferentiated hypotensive, not only the peri-arrest ones. That is the same territory CCPU examines, and it sits directly on top of the LITFL critical care ultrasound pages already in this feed. Better watched before your next shock case than after it.

items.title: "Half Framing" Practically Any Film Camera (Part 1 of 2)
items.summary: Turns half-frame into a technique you can run on a camera you already own instead of a second body you have to buy.

_homepage.note: The method needs nothing more than a double-exposure facility, which most of the usual suspects have, and it turns 36 exposures into 72 at a time when that arithmetic matters. 35mmc has twice earned a place in this feed on exactly this argument — use the camera you have, not the one you want. Part one is the method; the second half deals with what it does to scanning.

items.title: PlayStation State of Play September 2026: every reveal
items.summary: One page for everything Sony showed, and specifically for the dates that reorder a PS5 backlog.

_homepage.note: Final Fantasy Resonance took 22 October, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation went to April 2027, and Marvel's Wolverine was confirmed playable off a physical disc — a detail that carries weight given Sony is retiring PlayStation discs in 2028. Gran Turismo 7's Spec IV update splits across autumn and winter rather than landing at once. Skim it for dates, not trailers.

items.title: Jalen Ngonda on soul's timelessness and Doctrine of Love
items.summary: He is already on your shelf, and this is him explaining what he was reaching for on the record that follows.

_homepage.note: Doctrine of Love pushes past the orchestral sweep of the debut into horns and gospel-leaning backing vocals, with Chiarito and Buckley producing again for Daptone. The collection already holds Thee Sacred Souls, Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings and Menahan Street Band, so this is that same house sound moving forward rather than an unfamiliar bet. The interview catches him mid-tour, talking about why sixties soul still holds.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered: everything in the free upgrade
items.summary: A free upgrade to a game you almost certainly already own, with a date attached: 29 September.

_homepage.note: CD Projekt announced it at Gamescom for PC, PS5, Xbox Series and — natively for the first time — Switch 2, and anyone holding only the base game gets both expansions thrown in. PC Gamer's rundown is the one that lists what actually changed rather than replaying the trailer beats. Under four weeks out, so it is a decision about this month, not a wishlist item.

items.title: Banana Republic Archive Reissue Revives Safari Style
items.summary: Banana Republic has reissued its own safari-era archive — the exact thing you would otherwise be hunting secondhand.

_homepage.note: The Archive Reissue arrived with The Explorers Club and draws on the catalogue from the seventies through the early 2000s, which is the era vintage sellers have been pricing hard for years. Buying new is the cheap way to test whether those cuts actually work on you before chasing an original in the right size. Construction detail is thinner than Heddels would give you, but the reference points are the ones you already buy against.

items.title: Tochi Deli Reopens in Coburg, With the Same Great Sushi
items.summary: The Sydney Road sushi counter that vanished in July is trading again, ten minutes further north.

_homepage.note: Shingo and Rena Tochimoto ran the Brunswick market stall for five years before closing it; the Coburg room seats seventeen, sits across the mall from Half Moon, and carries the same nigiri, chirashi, donburi and onigiri at the same prices. Much of the fit-out is the old Brunswick timber unscrewed, sanded and reused. Northside, walkable from the 19, and cheap enough to be a weeknight rather than an occasion.

items.title: Higher risk PE management: STRATIFY and STORM-PE
items.summary: The two trials everyone is citing for intermediate-high-risk PE, read sceptically rather than reverentially.

_homepage.note: STORM-PE randomised only 100 patients and its primary outcome is RV/LV ratio at 48 hours — a surrogate, and Morgenstern says so plainly. STRATIFY's three-arm design (heparin alone versus catheter-directed versus systemic 20mg alteplase) is the one that matters for a department without an interventional service on site, which is most of them overnight. Worth reading before the guideline summaries harden into departmental policy.

items.title: EMCrit 424 – 2026 Crashing PE Update
items.summary: Weingart reconciles the AHA's A-to-E categories with the words you actually use at the bedside, then gives you an algorithm.

_homepage.note: The AHA's new alphabetic PE categories are the sort of thing that reads fine in a guideline and falls apart at 3am when the registrar has to say out loud what this patient is. This episode does the translation and then stratifies therapy across low-dose systemic lysis, mechanical thrombectomy, half-dose tenecteplase and ECMO, folding in STRATIFY and HI-PEITHO. Pair it with the First10EM appraisal of the same two trials, also in today's edition, and you have both the recommendation and the evidence behind it.

items.title: Research Roundup – June 2026
items.summary: A month of emergency medicine papers appraised in one sitting, with the weak ones named as weak.

_homepage.note: The monthly roundup is the cheapest way to stay current without reading journals, and it covers ground the podcasts skip — peripheral vasoactive administration among them, which is a live question in any department still moving pressors to a central line on principle. Skim the verdicts, read the two or three that touch your practice.

items.title: EMCrit 422 – SSC 2026 Sepsis Guidelines
items.summary: The lead author of the new Surviving Sepsis guidelines sits down and is asked which parts are actually bad.

_homepage.note: The 2026 rewrite carries 129 statements, 46 of them new ground, and it moves on things that change ED practice directly: high-flow nasal cannula as the first device in sepsis-associated respiratory failure, active fluid removal once resuscitation is done, and a recommendation against routine antipyretics. Having Hallie Prescott defend it live is more useful than reading the document, because the conditional recommendations are where the argument actually is.

items.title: Hermanos Gutiérrez Announce 'Los Ojos del Cóndor'
items.summary: The third Auerbach-produced record from a duo already on your shelf, out 25 September and worth a pre-order.

_homepage.note: Hermanos Gutiérrez are in the library, so this is a record to have on order rather than discover late. The pitch is a move off the American desert and into the Andes — Peru, their great-grandfather's country — which is a real change of vocabulary from El Bueno y el Malo and Sonido Cósmico rather than a third go at the same reverb. Dan Auerbach at Easy Eye again, which given what The Black Crowes and Menahan Street Band sit next to on your shelf is exactly the production register that suits it.

items.title: The Next Ascent
items.summary: What to work on once you can already expose correctly and the pictures still are not good.

_homepage.note: This is the plateau piece — written for the point where the mechanics are automatic and the limiting factor has become how you read light rather than what your meter says. The specific argument is about midtones and restraint, and about testing a stock properly instead of collecting stocks, which is a more useful discipline than another camera. Sits directly against the 35mmc one-camera piece already in your feed.

items.title: Eastman Kodak Goes Big and Shows Film Some More Love
items.summary: Tri-X 400 in 100-foot bulk rolls is back, which is the cheapest your black and white will ever get per frame.

_homepage.note: The headline is large format, but the line that matters for a 35mm shooter is the return of 100-foot bulk rolls of Tri-X 400 and Ektapan. Bulk loading is the one lever left on film cost now that per-roll prices have settled where they have, and this is the first time the newly in-house Eastman Kodak range has offered it. It also effectively closes out Kodak's move to take distribution back from Alaris, fourteen years on.

items.title: Internet Fashion Label Mutimer's Collingwood Store Opens
items.summary: Six years direct-to-consumer, and now there is finally somewhere in Melbourne to try the fit on.

_homepage.note: 308 Smith Street, so a tram ride rather than a postal gamble on sizing — which for a label you have only ever bought online is the whole point. Jasper Mutimer has fitted it out as a mid-century apartment, Eames chair and wall-mounted CD player included, which tells you how the brand wants the workwear read. Worth a walk down from Collingwood on a Saturday, and the closest thing Melbourne has to a home store for the label.

items.title: All About Flannel – Winter Fabric from Wales
items.summary: Why the word once meant wool, and how to tell a real flannel from a plaid-printed cotton shirt.

_homepage.note: Flannel is a nap and a finish, not a check — the pattern is the thing everyone mistakes for the cloth. The Welsh origin and the Pendleton century that followed are the useful part here, because Pendleton and Woolrich are the reference points you buy against, and both still trade on a wool flannel most of the market has quietly swapped for brushed cotton. Good reading going into a Melbourne spring, when the vintage racks fill with last winter's shirts.

items.title: Dragonwilds Leaves Early Access on 15 September 2026
items.summary: 1.0 lands in eleven days, on PS5 the same day as PC, with the Scorned Wilderness raid attached.

_homepage.note: First-party announcement rather than a re-write of it, so the platform detail is reliable: PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Switch 2 all on 15 September, with crossplay. 1.0 bundles the Scorned Wilderness raid, the Runite tier and the end of Kuldra's saga on top of everything from Umbral Sands. If you have been waiting to start on PlayStation rather than PC, this is the date to clear.

items.title: Enshrouded's release date set for October on PC and PS5
items.summary: The other survival game you have been waiting on console for — 15 October, PS5 and PS5 Pro, Xbox not until 2027.

_homepage.note: Two and a half years of early access ends on 15 October, and PlayStation gets it day one while Xbox waits until spring 2027. Keen are promising the parts early access never fixed — onboarding, quest flow, shader compilation stutter — plus Adventure Sharing, which opens other people's builds and trap-laden worlds to you. It lands a month after Dragonwilds 1.0, so October is a decision rather than a double buy.
